Q0559

“Happiness is the good desired for its own sake; it is never…” — Al-Farabi (The Attainment of Happiness)

Verified English quotation. Primary source: The Attainment of Happiness. Theme: happiness.

Quotes / Al-Farabi / Q0559

English

Happiness is the good desired for its own sake; it is never desired for the sake of something else.
Thinker Al-Farabi
School Islamic Philosophy
Source The Attainment of Happiness
Theme Happiness
Another quotation More from this thinker

Context and commentary are editorial aids for reading. They do not replace the primary text or scholarly commentary.

Source and attribution

The archive attributes this English wording to The Attainment of Happiness and files it under Islamic Philosophy. That locator distinguishes the passage from loose internet attributions: readers can return to the named work or section to check translation, surrounding argument, and edition-specific wording.

About Al-Farabi

Abū Naṣr al-Fārābī (c. 870–950), later called the ‘Second Teacher’ after Aristotle, worked mainly in Baghdad and Syria.

How to read this passage

Greek eudaimonia, Buddhist analyses of craving, utilitarian happiness, and modern well-being research all contest the meaning of a good life. This passage enters that discussion through happiness, good.

Concepts in this quote

Happiness
Happiness—or flourishing—is a central aim in ethics: what makes a life go well, and whether pleasure alone is enough.
Good
Good appears in this archive as a live philosophical concern—not a slogan. These verified English passages show how thinkers treat good as a problem of judgment, practice, or explanation.
